Synopsis:
A goblin who still follows the old goblin god, Maglubiyet, while the rest of his tribe have started to follow a new god, the Absolute. He sees them as heretics - they think the same of him, and have locked him in a cage.

Cluster Contexts:
- GOB_GoblinHeretic.json: Brakkal is a goblin prisoner who refuses to renounce the old goblin god Maglubiyet; his own tribe has embraced a new deity, the Absolute, and locked him in a cage as a heretic. He’s furious and defiant—chanting prayers to Maglubiyet, sneering at the converts, and warning the player the tribe will turn on them. Off‑screen the rest of the tribe is loyal to the Absolute and hostile to dissent, so any attempt to free or provoke Brakkal could quickly spark violence. The narrator’s note that Maglubiyet is a tyrannical, slave‑driving deity explains Brakkal’s fierce, bitter conviction.
- GOB_GoblinHeretic_Saved.json: The goblin is a lone believer in the old goblin god Maglubiyet whose tribe has converted to the Absolute and imprisoned him as a heretic. Off‑screen the players have just freed him from a cage and dealt with his captors, so he’s reacting to being rescued and to seeing those attackers dead or defeated. He thanks the party, bitterly rejects his former tribe as heretics, and says he’ll go find a new group that still honors the old ways. The sample lines show gleeful vindication at the fate of the Absolute followers and a grateful, friendly tone toward his rescuers; how this plays out can vary with the player’s prior actions.
- FOR_GnomeGoblin2.json: The party arrives at a windmill where three goblins have captured a gnome and are spinning him around for sport; the gnome is tied and being actively tormented off‑screen. Fezzerk is the leader and the primary speaker, while GnomeGobllin2 is one of two lackeys who either hisses threats or grovels when intimidated (notably by a drow in the party). By default the goblins are belligerent and enjoy bullying—they’ll fight unless placated or convinced otherwise. If the player recovered the amulet of the Conquering God from the wilderness priests, it can be used as a bargaining tool to sway or intimidate the goblins.
- GOB_GuardTense.json: A petty goblin guard posted inside a temple, a bit more relaxed and jokey than his zealous companion, who is likely the one with authority to grant passage. He habitually sniffs and comments on a visitor’s smell (burns, booze) and offers brusque, "beginner" advice or mockery while remaining on duty. If you try to pass without his superior’s permission he will refuse and quickly escalate to threats or combat. Off‑screen reactions that explain his mood include being seen looting a corpse or chest, trespassing, or having witnesses (goblin kids, agents, druids) nearby—those prior actions determine whether he warns, detains, or attacks.
- FOR_GnomeGoblin1.json: The party finds three goblins tormenting a bound deep gnome (Barcus Wroot) by tying him to a windmill sail and jeering as he spins; Fezzerk is the boastful leader who taunts the captive and demands an absurd “toll” from anyone who tries to pass. If the player bears a cult symbol/True Soul mark it can glow and intimidate Fezzerk into withdrawing, though using that mark produces an unsettling, hunger‑like reaction in the player. Goblins react to PC race — a drow player will make them far more nervous and easier to cow. The captive occasionally cries out (pleading, panicked, or insulting), and off‑screen there may be wider goblin activity and refugee/druid tensions in the region that don’t need to be resolved to play this scene.

context: Brakkal is a goblin prisoner who refuses to renounce the old goblin god Maglubiyet; his own tribe has converted to the Absolute and locked him in a cage as a heretic. He’s furious and defiant, loudly chanting praise to Maglubiyet (a tyrannical, slave‑driving deity, per the narrator) and sneering at those who abandoned the old ways. Off‑screen the rest of the tribe are loyal Absolute worshippers and hostile to dissent, so attempts to free or provoke Brakkal can quickly spark violence.
